parent: Training-selected event-driven breakout policy: entry_window=40, stop_atr=3.5, entry_cap=0.7, exit_style=trailing. Preserve its complete 36-candidate ledger and retrospective results.
hypothesis: A normal holding trail should tolerate early trend noise, but the same distance surrenders excessive profit after a fast price extension. Tighten the ratcheted stop only after an objectively observed large multi-session gain, and separately test whether breadth confirmation blocks false breakout purchases in a declining technology basket.
protection: After current close / close[heat_window sessions ago] - 1 exceeds heat_gain, ratchet the observed holding's stop to at least peak * (1-hot_drawdown). Stop cannot loosen on a later volatility spike or when heat dissipates. Fresh closing damage triggers a sell for next open; no intraday or peak-price fill. Risk always precedes entry.
entry_gate: For breadth variant only: fresh entries require at least half of currently ready input names above their twenty-session mean; existing intact holdings are never sold solely because breadth declines. No outside symbols or excluded leaders enter the breadth calculation.
selection_objective: mean(log(wealth / matched buy_hold wealth) - 0.75 * max_drawdown - 0.002 * max(0, orders_per_year - 20))
evidence: Bound both parent policy and extension source bytes, config, runner and data. Preserve all attempted candidates, including failures and source-only testing errors. Already-observed historical evaluation is retrospective, not prospective proof. No production dates, security identifiers or phase/version labels. Accounting, capacity and fee assumptions unchanged.
